newsitem.title: CANADA: Morrison CEO sees C$10/shr bid failing.
newsitem.headline: Morrison CEO sees C$10/shr bid failing.

text.p: Gordon Stollery, chairman and chief executive of takeover target Morrison Petroleums Ltd, said on Monday he was confident that Canadian 88 Energy Corp's C$10 per share bid would fail.

"Let me put it this way: I haven't talked to a single person who is going to tender at C$10. And I've talked to quite a few arbitragers, I've talked to lots of shareholders -- so I suspect the C$10 bid will fail," Stollery said in an interview.

Morrison's board of directors on Monday urged shareholders to reject Canadian 88's C$652 million hostile offer because it did not give enough value to the company's oil and gas reserves, landholdings, investments and prospects.

"The offer does not take into account the superior growth prospects which exist for Morrison resulting from its three-year strategy of land accumulation, exploration drilling, and acquisition and construction of strategic facilities," the company said in a statement.

Stollery said he believed that a competing offer for his firm was the most likely outcome of the takeover battle, which began earlier this month when Canadian 88 offered C$10 cash, up to a maximum of C$140 million, or 1.5 of its shares for each Morrison share.
He said various firms had signed confidentiality agreements and begun to scour the company's proprietary financial and operating data. Other companies planned to enter the data room soon, he said.

Interest in acquiring Morrison has come from Canadian, U.S. and international firms, although few had established operating positions in Alberta's foothills, where Morrison has focused recent operations, Stollery said.
CIBC Wood Gundy analyst Peter Linder said he believed that given the bright investment outlook in Canada's oil and gas industry, interest in acquiring Morrison would be strong.

"I've said from Day One that there's got to be a lot of interest in this company in this very good environment," Linder said. "They'll soon have to start selling tickets to get in (Morrison's data room)."
Morrison shares closed down C$0.05 to C$10.30 on volume of 1.06 million shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday. Canadian 88's stock fell C$0.05 to close at C$6.50 on 217,000 shares.
